how_it_spreads.value: eating contaminated ready-to-eat chicken salad sold at grocery store delis

key_symptoms.value: diarrhea, fever and abdominal cramps starting 12 to 72 hours after exposure, usually lasting 4 to 7 days

mortality.value: 1 death and 94 hospitalizations among 265 confirmed cases

treatment_overview.value: mild cases usually resolve with fluid and electrolyte replacement; severe cases may need hospitalization, IV fluids and antibiotics, especially if the infection spreads to the bloodstream

summary.value: This 2018 outbreak was caused by Salmonella Typhimurium in ready-to-eat chicken salad sold at Iowa grocery stores, sickening 265 people across 8 states and causing one death. It shows how poultry products contaminated with Salmonella can cause serious illness in people even after the bird itself has been processed.
